def best_screening_plan(k, films):
    """Choose which films to screen on k identical projectors.

    A festival owns k identical projectors (0 <= k <= 50).  films is a
    list of n candidate screenings (0 <= n <= 200); each screening is a
    tuple (s, e, w) of ints with 0 <= s < e <= 10**9 and
    1 <= w <= 10**6, meaning it occupies the half-open time interval
    [s, e) and earns revenue w.  Equal tuples may appear several times
    and count as separate screenings.

    A plan is any subset of the screenings such that at every time
    instant t the number of chosen screenings with s <= t < e is at
    most k.  Equivalently: the chosen screenings can be distributed
    among the k projectors so that no projector shows two films whose
    intervals share an interior point (one film may end at time t and
    another start at the same t on the same projector).  The empty plan
    is always valid.

    Return a tuple (r, c) of two ints: r is the maximum total revenue
    over all plans, and c is the smallest number of screenings used by
    any plan whose revenue equals r.  If k == 0 or films is empty,
    return (0, 0).

    The bounds are small, but exhaustive search over the 2**n subsets
    is hopeless and simple greedy or single-projector DP strategies are
    wrong for k >= 2; an exact polynomial-time algorithm is required.

    >>> best_screening_plan(1, [(0, 3, 5), (2, 5, 4), (4, 7, 5)])
    (10, 2)
    >>> best_screening_plan(1, [(0, 4, 5), (0, 2, 3), (2, 4, 2)])
    (5, 1)
    >>> best_screening_plan(2, [(0, 10, 4), (1, 9, 4), (2, 8, 4), (3, 7, 4)])
    (8, 2)
    """
